test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains travelling in the same direction at 40 km/h and 22 km/h cross each other completely in 1 minute. If the length of the first train is 125 m, what is the length of the second train?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 40 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 22 km/h

Time (t) = 1 minute = 1/60 hour

Length of first train (L₁) = 125 m

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in same direction) = S₁ - S₂

Distance covered = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed = 40 km/h - 22 km/h = 18 km/h

Convert Relative Speed to m/s: 18 km/h = 18 × (5/18) m/s = 5 m/s

Distance covered (total length of both trains) = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Distance covered = 5 m/s × (1/60) hour × 3600 seconds/hour = 300 m

Total length of both trains = 300 m

Length of second train (L₂) = Total length - Length of first train

⇒ L₂ = 300 m - 125 m

⇒ L₂ = 175 m

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
